name: Pável Mwangi-Szczepanik
description: A corporate-owned neural-feed actor who disappeared from public record in 2209 at the height of his career, Mwangi-Szczepanik was known for villains and morally compromised protagonists whose neural signatures produced what audiences called 'comfortable dread' — an addictive unease that Vantablack licensed widely for thriller and crime content. Of Kenyan-Polish descent with significant chrome augmentation including a full-skull subdermal lattice visible beneath the skin, he was one of Vantablack's most commercially valuable assets. His disappearance was officially attributed to voluntary retirement and a private health matter.
cultural_impact: His absence from the feed became its own cultural event, spawning a devoted community of investigators whose theories about what happened to him have never been officially refuted.
story_hooks: Someone claiming to be him makes contact through a Shelf dead-drop network, sending a fragment of neural-feed that contains information only he could know — and it is clearly a plea.

A journalist investigating his disappearance finds that his neural signature is still being actively licensed two years after his 'retirement,' generating revenue for Vantablack with no payment going to any known account.
His chrome augmentation contained a passive recording function he may not have known about — and someone in the Shelf claims to have recovered years of archived data from a fragment of the lattice.
